findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: Inspector observed no certified food protection manager present during today’s inspection. The facility does have two CFPM’s on staff, but one alternates between locations and the other was away taking some children from the daycare on a field trip. The PIC was informed that a CFPM must be present at all times of food preparation. Ensure more staff members receive certification prior to next routine inspection to accommodate for trips/illness/unexpected staffing complications.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Inspector observed shredded cheese, hotdogs, sliced cheese, and deli meat to be stored in the facility longer than 24 hours without a date mark. The PIC was informed and date marking was added to these items. No items were kept longer than 7 days. Ensure all time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods are marked with the date of opening and discarded after 7 days.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.comment: Inspector observed plastic serving plates stored without protective covering on a high shelf in the kitchen. To protect the food contact surfaces of these items, ensure the plates are inverted (face-down on the clean shelf) to prevent contamination from dust, splash, or other debris.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: Inspector observed a ceiling tile over the glass front cooler to be stained with what appears to be a historical water spot. The tile is dry but bowed. Replace the ceiling tile before the next routine inspection. 

PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.
